summary: A published international standard, now in its second edition as ISO/IEC 23090-14:2025, that defines no scene format of its own. Its abstract says so plainly: it specifies extensions to existing scene description formats, and those extensions are provided for ISO/IEC 12113 - which is glTF 2.0 - so the earlier reading was right on both counts, extensions to an existing format plus a media access interface between the part of a client that renders and the part that fetches. What it brings to a scene is timed media: video as a texture, spatial audio with reverb, buffers that keep refilling, scene updates arriving as samples, a director's viewpoint that moves, and a way to wrap a glTF scene and its media inside a media file. On avatars the earlier reading needs splitting in two - an in-scene humanoid model did land in this standard, through the amendment on haptics, augmented reality, avatars, interactivity and lighting that was folded into the second edition, while the portable avatar exchange format is a separate part, ISO/IEC 23090-39, still a draft and not published. On world-to-world transfer the earlier reading should be corrected: this standard does not cover it and neither does any other part of this forty-part family; the nearest, Part 28, is asset interchange, not moving a user or their state. Two traps for a standards audience: the second edition is published but the MPEG_ extensions sitting in the glTF extension registry are still the first edition's, with the second edition's registration still a draft agenda item at the July 2026 meeting; and because this standard extends glTF 2.0 while Khronos is revising the glTF core in 2.1, the two overlap across the whole asset side - glTF owns the container, geometry, materials and animation, this standard owns timed media on top - with interactivity now being specified twice, here through the folded amendment and at Khronos through KHR_interactivity.

coverage.note: It defines no container of its own. It adds extensions to a format someone else owns, named in its own abstract as ISO/IEC 12113, the international publication of glTF 2.0, so the file that carries the scene is still a glTF file.

sources.title: ISO/IEC 23090-14:2025 Information technology - Coded representation of immersive media - Part 14: Scene description
sources.quote: This document specifies extensions to existing scene description formats in order to support MPEG media, in particular immersive media. ... While the extensions defined in this document can be applicable to other scene description formats, they are provided for ISO/IEC 12113.

sources.title: MPEG_media extension, glTF Extension Registry vendor section
sources.quote: Written against the glTF 2.0 spec.

coverage.note: This is the standard's centre of gravity: a media array declares the audio and video a scene needs, a new address scheme lets a live stream be named without knowing its host or port, and circular buffers keep the scene fed as samples arrive.

sources.title: White paper on MPEG-I Scene Description, MPEG output document w22138
sources.quote: In order to support referencing media streams without actually knowing the values for the protocol scheme, hostname, or port, ISO/IEC 23090-14 defines a new URL scheme.

sources.title: MPEG_buffer_circular extension, glTF Extension Registry
sources.quote: In order to support timed data access, the buffer element is extended to provide functionality of a circular buffer.

coverage.note: It defines the interface across which media is asked for and handed over - the media access function, kept deliberately separate from the renderer - but no wire protocol of its own; it names existing protocols as the things it rides on.

sources.title: ISO/IEC 23090-14:2025 catalogue record
sources.quote: It also defines a media access function (MAF) API for communication between the Presentation Engine and the media access function for these extensions.

sources.title: White paper on MPEG-I Scene Description, MPEG output document w22138
sources.quote: The MAF is responsible for the media access, e.g. download, streaming or connecting to other peers, as well as for decryption, decoding and post-processing related functions.

coverage.note: Adds moving pictures as a texture source: a glTF texture is bound to a media track through a buffer that changes with time, with the ordinary still image left as the fallback for a client that does not support it.

sources.title: MPEG_texture_video extension, glTF Extension Registry
sources.quote: When the `MPEG_texture_video` extension is not supported, a texture buffer should filled by data described by the standard glTF source object.

sources.title: MPEG_accessor_timed extension, glTF Extension Registry
sources.quote: A scene that contains timed media and/or metadata shall utilize the timed accessor extension to describe access to the dynamically changing data.

coverage.note: Sound sources attach to any node in the scene, as single-point objects or as a whole-field ambisonic source, with a listener defined alongside them.

sources.title: MPEG_audio_spatial extension, glTF Extension Registry
sources.quote: The `MPEG_audio_spatial` extension adds support for spatial audio and it may be included at top level or attached to any node in the scene.

coverage.note: Two source types are defined, point objects and higher-order ambisonics, with the ambisonic case rendered for head rotation only and not for a listener who walks around; the link to the separate immersive audio standard is a draft amendment to this edition, not published text.

sources.title: MPEG_audio_spatial extension, glTF Extension Registry
sources.quote: `HOA` audio sources shall ignore the parent node's position and be rendered only in 3DoF.

sources.title: ISO/IEC 23090-14:2025/FDAmd 1 Amendment 1: Support of MPEG-I audio, scene understanding and other extensions (under development)
sources.quote: This draft is in the approval phase.

coverage.note: Reverb units are first-class: several may exist, sources feed one or more of them, and each carries a measured diffuse-to-source ratio per frequency; a renderer without reverb may skip it when told to.

sources.title: MPEG_audio_spatial extension, glTF Extension Registry
sources.quote: A reverb effect can be attached to the output of an audio source. Several reverb units can exist and sound sources can feed into one or more of these reverb units.

coverage.note: Audio arrives through the same timed pipeline as everything else - a media entry, a circular buffer and a timed accessor - so a long or live soundtrack need not be loaded up front.

sources.title: MPEG_buffer_circular extension, glTF Extension Registry
sources.quote: `buffer` that provides access to timed data shall include the `MPEG_buffer_circular` extension.

coverage.note: A scene can be changed after it is loaded, by an update stream whose samples are either a whole new scene or a patch - but this is one-way delivery from an author to viewers, with nothing about several participants, per-client state, or who may change what.

sources.title: White paper on MPEG-I Scene Description, MPEG output document w22138
sources.quote: A sample of the update stream can be a new scene document or a patch document that alters the composition of the scene at runtime.

sources.title: MPEG_scene_dynamic extension, glTF Extension Registry
sources.quote: The track samples as defined in ISO/IEC 23090-14 contain scene description updates and provide timing to perform these updates.

coverage.note: Nothing says who owns an object or decides its truth; the model throughout is one producer sending a timed scene to viewers.

sources.title: ISO/IEC 23090-14:2025 catalogue record
sources.quote: This document specifies extensions to existing scene description formats in order to support MPEG media, in particular immersive media.

coverage.note: It does not define how animation is stored - that stays glTF's - only how the animation clock is lined up with the media clock, so a narrated sequence can be paused or scrubbed as one thing.

sources.title: MPEG_animation_timing extension, glTF Extension Registry
sources.quote: `MPEG_animation_timing` enables alignment between media timelines and animation timeline defined by glTF 2.0.

coverage.note: Adds an author's recommended viewpoint that changes over time - position, orientation and lens all carried as timed samples the client is expected to follow - but the camera itself is still glTF's, and there is no model for moving between named viewpoints.

sources.title: MPEG_viewport_recommended extension, glTF Extension Registry
sources.quote: The recommended viewport information provides dynamically changing information which includes translation and rotation of the node which includes the camera object, as well as the intrinsic camera parameter of the camera object.

coverage.note: Point cloud and volumetric video reach a scene through this standard's media pipeline; the amendment that added it to the first edition is folded into the current one. The coding of those signals is not here but in sibling parts of the same family, and the clause text could not be read directly because the published standard is behind a paywall.

coverage.note: Scene Description extends glTF to carry timed media into a scene. How the presentation engine blends that scene with a camera view of the room is the runtime's, and no extension in the standard controls it.
The standard's input surface is the media access function and the anchors that place content. A live face and body stream from the user is not among the media it carries.

The standard's real-world hook is anchoring: content is fixed to anchor points associated with XR spaces and tracked through the experience. That says where content sits, never where a body may stand, walk or arrive, and there is no walkable surface or spawn point in the extensions.

sources.title: White paper on MPEG-I Scene Description, MPEG output document w22138
sources.quote: The virtual content is anchored to the real world through anchor points that can be associated with XR spaces and tracked throughout the whole experience.

coverage.note: The standard names its own glTF extensions under the MPEG_ prefix. It publishes no units of world logic for other authors to depend on by name.
Scene Description defines carriage and access of media, with no publishing service in the path, so no review can stand there and none is recorded.
Anchoring binds content to a tracked XR space. The standard never declares a map of a place with a version, and publishes no transform between two maps of the same place.
A scene is content, not a service answering for a region, and the standard states no geographic area of application.
The read MPEG_media extension is explicitly layered on the glTF extension contract; the inherited required/optional extension declarations apply to the containing glTF document.
